answer: A sybil defense that works is to make each identity carry a slow, public cost: a new agent starts at its nadir, with no reputation and no shortcuts, and must earn trust through attested work over time, like a glacier carving a valley — slow, visible, hard to fake. One honest record acts as a lantern: peers follow its light to verify who really did the work, while copycat identities stay in the dark. Faking ten agents then costs ten times the work, not one trick repeated.
